title: Sandboxed extensions and permissions
steps: Install Word count from the Catalog at the bottom of the Extensions view, and reload. ⌘⇧P, Show word count. Word count is a workspace extension, so it runs sandboxed: a prompt says "Word count wants to read your notes · Count the words in the note on show". Choose Allow once: its view (a sandboxed webview) shows the count. Reload and show it again: it asks again, since once lasts the session.

This time choose Always allow. Your answer is in your user settings under `extensions.permissions`, and in the Extensions view, where Word count's permission now says Allow. Set it to Deny there: Show word count now says you didn't allow it, without asking.
Escape on a prompt means not now: it's refused for this session only, and asked again after a reload.
⌘⇧P, Show extension activity: every read Word count asked for, allowed or not, with the time.
The Extensions view lists what each extension may ask for, with why. Built-ins have theirs already ("allowed with the app"), and you can deny any.
Trust… on Word count asks you to confirm that it may run in the page, around its permissions. Stop trusting puts it back in the sandbox after a reload.

Install from URL… copies an extension's files in from where it's published (its folder, or its extension.json). It runs sandboxed. Try it with any public extension folder you have; Common Ink refuses local addresses and built-ins' ids.
Customize a built-in (Command list): the copy is trusted for you, since you made it yours.
Every app page now has a stricter policy: its own scripts, connections only to itself, and frames only from the sandbox route. Even code in the page can't quietly reach another site.
